name: usage
documentation: Per-request counters and gauges, flushed to the queue at after.execute and applied to hourly buckets by a worker, then rolled up into daily ones. The request path never performs the durable write: it adds to an in-memory accumulator and, once the response exists, pushes ONE queue message. Appwrite runs its metering queue at 8 coroutines precisely because it fires on every request; a synchronous write here would tax every response.
//enabling-it-for-every-request: The after.execute hook is registered globally by boot(), so request counts (http.requests, http.errors, http.bytes_out) are recorded for every route whether or not this module is in the route's dependency graph. A route that wants to call UsageContract (count/gauge from a service) declares "requires": ["usage.metering"]. Reads (sum, growth, latest) need a DatabasePort in the graph or on the core container.
//needs-a-queue-and-a-worker: With no QueuePort bound the stage drops the batch — it does NOT fall back to writing inline, because that fallback is the cost this design exists to avoid. `usage:show` prints the line either way; a stopped worker shows as every metric going flat, not as an error.
//tenant-is-attribution: The tenant id on a measurement comes from Identity::tenantId, which is a hint. It decides which row a count lands on and authorises nothing.
